A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GeoRCG and contain readable main text and appendices A–F. Text extraction, rendered pages, and matching figures support a reliable comparison, including material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original unconditional and conditional molecule-generation experiments on QM9 and GEOM-DRUG, reduced-step results, and encoder and representation-perturbation ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds results for GeoRCG with SemlaFlow and reduced-step generation on GEOM-DRUG.

M1.justification: The two-stage framework and EDM formulation remain unchanged. V2 adds a SemlaFlow adaptation with cross-attention between Semla blocks and an auxiliary MSE loss between representations of denoised and ground-truth molecules (Appendix C). This is a concrete but localized methodological extension.

E1.justification: Downstream coverage remains QM9, GEOM-DRUG, and the same six conditional properties. However, Section 4.1 changes Uni-Mol pretraining from GEOM-DRUG itself to adding GEOM-DRUG to its pretraining dataset. The other corpus and relationship to v1's training are unspecified, leaving any training-data coverage change unresolved.

E2.justification: V2 Table 3 adds SemlaFlow and EQGAT-diff as evaluated comparators and includes MiDi in the new GEOM-DRUG comparison. The original comparator sets remain, including MiDi and LDM-3DG in the QM9 geometry comparison moved from v1 Table 2 to v2 Table 7.

E3.justification: The new SemlaFlow evaluation uses 5,000 sampled molecules and adds MMFF94 energy and strain-energy metrics, including relaxation in RDKit. V2 also adds a 50/100/500/1,000-step GEOM-DRUG evaluation. Existing EDM settings and conditional splits remain; the QM9 reduced-step table no longer reports valid-and-unique scores.

E4.justification: V2 extends the diffusion-step sensitivity analysis from QM9 to GEOM-DRUG (Table 4), while dropping uniqueness outcomes from the QM9 sweep. Encoder, perturbation/dropout, controllability, novelty, and representation-fit analyses remain; moving existing analyses into Appendix D does not constitute new evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report default three-run averages with standard errors. V2 specifies five-run averaging for the added SemlaFlow comparison (Table 3). This is new experiment-specific reporting, not evidence that existing experiments received additional runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial result sets for SemlaFlow and GEOM-DRUG step sensitivity while retaining the original headline tables. Table 3 reports GeoRCG/SemlaFlow validity of 95.1/94.0%, energy of 87.86/93.72, and strain of 47.07/52.98 kcal/mol. Reduced-step QM9 uniqueness entries disappear. New Table 4's 1,000-step GeoBFN stability/validity values, 85.6/92.08%, differ without explanation from retained Table 1's 86.1/91.66%.

T1.justification: Appendix E adds Assumption E.13 and Theorem E.14 with a proof extending the analysis to permutation and SE(3) symmetries, zero-center-of-mass Gaussian noise, and separate coordinate and atom-feature score errors. V2 also changes dimensional factors in existing bounds from d+3 to N(d+3). These extend the mathematics beyond renumbering.

C1.justification: V2 adds a specific claim of enhancing SemlaFlow on GEOM-DRUG and restricts the quality–diversity contribution to QM9. The abstract softens the 100-step claim from superior quality to largely preserving 1,000-step quality. The 31% conditional-generation claim remains. The new 'across all metrics' improvement claim exceeds the displayed evidence because atom stability ties at 99.9%.

C2.justification: V1 emphasizes inadequate encoder pretraining, dataset diversity, and nonequilibrium structures when explaining GEOM-DRUG limitations. V2 instead emphasizes EDM's limited capacity in the main results discussion. Its limitations discussion links weak representations specifically to reduced benefits from low-temperature sampling and classifier-free guidance.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds SemlaFlow implementation details: cross-attention placement, batch cost 2048, 300 epochs, representation noise 0.3, auxiliary-loss weight 0.5, and sampling parameters (w,T)=(-0.9,1.0). It also documents MMFF94 energy and relaxation calculations. Existing EDM architecture, hardware, and training-time disclosures remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations including EQGAT-diff, UniGEM, guided flows, the GEOM dataset paper, and a data-processing-inequality proof, while removing GeoDiff. SemlaFlow was already cited in v1 but becomes a tested base generator. The principal positioning relative to RCG, GraphRCG, and latent molecular generators remains.

P1.justification: The section sequence and much of the prose remain. Local revisions update the abstract, baseline descriptions, and limitations; controllability and QM9 geometry discussions move to Appendix D. V2 also adds equal-contribution credit and an Impact Statement and reformats the algorithm description.

P2.justification: V2 converts the main text and references to two columns and substantially resizes and redistributes displays. Existing representation and controllability figures move into the appendix, and v1 Table 2 becomes appendix Table 7. Two new tables are added, and the QM9 reduced-step table loses a column and its redundant summary row. Existing figure imagery is retained.

improvement.justification: V1 left integration with stronger generators as future work. V2's SemlaFlow comparison, including energy and strain measurements, provides useful evidence for applicability beyond EDM, while Appendix E adds molecule-specific analysis. This strengthens an already supported framework. The net gain is limited by omitted reduced-step uniqueness results, unclear pretraining-data changes, and unexplained differences between GeoBFN values in Tables 1 and 4.
